title: Graph RAG / Knowledge Graphs
summary: Combine entity relationships with source passages to answer connection-oriented questions that isolated similarity matches cannot resolve.
overview: Graph RAG uses an explicit relationship representation to guide retrieval or synthesis. A knowledge graph can represent suppliers, facilities, products, incidents, and their connections; linked source passages provide the evidence behind each node or edge. Some GraphRAG approaches additionally build community summaries for corpus-wide questions. These are design choices, not a single interchangeable algorithm.

The graph is a derived evidence structure, not unquestionable truth. Entity resolution, relation extraction, temporal validity, and provenance determine its usefulness. A graph traversal can expose a possible path, but the answer must distinguish asserted relationships from inferred connections and must respect permissions on every contributing source.

production.poc: A prototype models one narrow relationship question and manually checks extracted entities and edges.
production.production: Production attaches provenance, confidence, validity intervals, and access metadata while evaluating both extraction and retrieval.
production.scale: Enterprise scale requires incremental graph updates, entity merge governance, traversal limits, and recomputation rules for summaries affected by source changes.

components.name: Entity resolver
components.role: Maps mentions to stable identities while preserving ambiguous matches.

components.name: Relation extractor
components.role: Produces typed edges with source evidence and temporal attributes.

components.name: Graph store
components.role: Supports bounded traversal and relationship filtering.

components.name: Passage index
components.role: Retrieves original text supporting graph nodes and edges.

components.name: Graph-guided retriever
components.role: Combines traversal results, source passages, and optional community summaries.

flow.title: Ingest evidence
flow.description: Parse documents and retain immutable source identifiers and access metadata.

flow.title: Resolve entities
flow.description: Link mentions conservatively and quarantine uncertain merges.

flow.title: Build supported relations
flow.description: Store typed edges with evidence, validity, and extraction version.

flow.title: Plan traversal
flow.description: Choose allowed relation types, depth, and temporal scope for the question.

flow.title: Retrieve supporting passages
flow.description: Fetch authorized source text for the selected path or community.

flow.title: Synthesize with qualifications
flow.description: Cite relationships and identify uncertainty instead of presenting inferred edges as established facts.

diagrams.title: Repairing graph evidence after source change
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant S as Source registry
 participant X as Extraction pipeline
 participant G as Graph store
 participant R as Retriever
 S->>X: Source revision or deletion
 X->>G: Invalidate dependent edges
 X->>G: Write validated replacement relations
 R->>G: Query at requested validity time
 G-->>R: Paths with current provenance
 R->>S: Fetch authorized supporting passages
diagrams.caption: Graph updates must follow source lineage so obsolete relationships and summaries can be repaired.

useCase.title: Tracing a shared upstream dependency
useCase.situation: A manufacturer investigates whether several delayed parts depend on the same upstream processing facility.
useCase.problem: Part-level document search finds separate supplier notes but does not connect their facility references.
useCase.requirement: Expose the dependency path with dated evidence and uncertainty.
useCase.architecture: A graph connects suppliers, facilities, and parts; each edge links to an approved source passage.
runtime: The question resolves affected part IDs and traverses supplier-to-facility edges.
The agent fetches supporting notes and reports a shared facility only where the evidence supports it.
useCase.failure: An ambiguous facility name remains two possible entities until reviewed, preventing a false shared-dependency conclusion.
useCase.impact: Measure supported-path precision, entity-resolution errors, and evidence freshness; graph density alone is not a quality metric.

tradeoffs.cost: Can obscure source-level detail and become stale.

failures.detection: Unrelated organizations share an apparent dependency.
failures.recovery: Split the entity and recompute affected edges and summaries.

failures.detection: A traversal uses an obsolete supplier relationship.
failures.recovery: Filter by validity interval and reconcile source updates.

mistakes.fix: Limit depth, relation types, and result cardinality.
Authorize every contributing source or build scope-specific summaries.

whenToUse: Use for dependency, ownership, and relationship questions.
Use when repeated entity connections matter across documents.
Use for corpus-level synthesis with maintained provenance.
whenNotToUse: Avoid graphs for simple isolated fact lookup.
Avoid automatic entity merging without quality controls.
Do not deploy when source relationships cannot be kept current.
checklist: Evaluate supported paths against expert labels.
